Chapter 3: The Power of Covenants—God’s Promises and Our Commitments
Have you ever been let down by a promise? Maybe a friend didn’t come through, or a parent broke a vow, or even a goal you set for yourself just slipped away. In those moments, the idea of a covenant—a sacred promise between God and His children—can feel almost out of reach. But in the Book of Mormon, covenants aren’t some distant concept. They’re actually the heartbeat of a relationship with God.
Imagine a group of people gathered by a river, getting ready for baptism. Their clothes are plain, and you can see both anxiety and hope on their faces. They’re not just there to follow a rule—they’ve come to make a promise. Not just to God, but to each other. The water’s cold, the experience might feel a little strange, but something sacred is happening. In that moment, the covenant isn’t just words. It’s a new beginning—a chance to start fresh.
The prophets in the Book of Mormon knew just how central covenants are to God’s plan. Every promise God makes, He keeps—always, through Christ. Think back to the ancient Israelites with their sacrifices and rituals. Those old covenants were powerful, but the Book of Mormon helps us see they were always meant to point forward, to the moment Christ’s atonement would make forgiveness and real change possible for everyone.
Most people don’t realize how personal these covenants really are. They’re not just for a group or a nation. They’re invitations to each of us—no matter where we come from or what we’ve done. Remember Alma, one of the Book of Mormon’s most memorable leaders? He invites his people to make a covenant at the waters of Mormon. He doesn’t sugarcoat it or promise an easy life. Instead, he calls them to “mourn with those that mourn,” to “bear one another’s burdens,” and to be “witnesses of God at all times.” It’s a big commitment, but the reward? A whole new identity as God’s people.
But here’s something to really pay attention to: Covenants in the Book of Mormon aren’t just about obedience. They’re about transformation. When people keep their promises to God, something changes inside them. They become more patient, more compassionate, and more willing to forgive. It’s not always easy. There are setbacks, doubts, and moments when it feels impossible. But the covenant stays—a steady reminder that God’s promises hold true, even when ours slip.
And if you’re feeling unworthy or uncertain, you’re not alone. The Book of Mormon reassures us: God’s covenants aren’t just for the perfect. They’re for anyone who’s willing to try, to repent, and to trust in Christ’s grace. The stories in its pages are full of people who messed up, who doubted, who struggled to keep their commitments. But every time, they found that God was faithful—even when they weren’t.
So, in a world where promises get broken every day, the Book of Mormon’s message couldn’t be more clear. God’s covenants are real. They’re fulfilled through Christ. And if you’re searching for hope, healing, or a fresh start, that promise is just as real for you today as it was for those ancient believers by the river.
